items.title: Claude Code 2.1.317 adds email send check, hook failure blocking, and Read tool changes
facts: Added a check that asks before a web or shell tool call sends your account email address to the network
Added onFailure: "block" for Agent SDK hook callbacks, so a callback that fails blocks the action instead of letting it run
Removed the Read tool's "file unchanged since your last Read" stub: reading an unchanged file again returns its content

x_posts.author: @cryptokoala_
x_posts.text:
Claude Code 2.1.317 has been released.

87 changes

Highlights:
• A check now asks before tool calls send your account email
• Agent SDK hook callbacks support onFailure: "block"
• Fixed Ctrl+C at the prompt stopping all background agents

https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.317

Claude Code 2.1.317 just dropped, here's what matters

> Asks before a web or shell tool call sends your account email over the network

items.title: Antigravity CLI ships v1.4.4–v1.4.12 with Auto mode, sandbox hardening, and streaming gains
facts: Enabled Auto mode on Windows 11 version 24H2 and later for personal Google Accounts, selectable via --mode auto, Agent Mode in /config, Shift+Tab, or Remote Control Settings (Agent remains the default).
Sandboxed commands can no longer read or modify ~/.docker, ~/.kube, or ~/_netrc unless you grant access explicitly.
Streaming writes about 70% fewer bytes to the terminal and stays much smoother over slow SSH connections.

items.title: Community shares experimental Claude Code agent teams setup with Opus lead and Sonnet teammates
facts: Launch Claude Code with experimental agent teams enabled like this: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 claude --model opus
Opus 5.5 runs the session, plans the feature and coordinates the work
Sonnet 5.5 teammates build in parallel: frontend, backend and integration

x_posts.author: @hayatomaruu
x_posts.text:
THIS IS AN ACTUAL F*CKING GOLDMINE

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 teammates at once, each one doing only the job you assign it.

Parallel work and less clutter in the lead's context, because every task lands on the right teammate.

You just launch Claude Code with experimental agent teams enabled like this:

CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 claude --model opus

here's the split:

→ Opus 5.5 runs the session, plans the feature and coordinates the work
→ Sonnet 5.5 teammates build in parallel: frontend, backend and integration
→ the shared task list tracks ownership, progress and dependencies
→ you stop burning Opus context on implementation work Sonnet can handle

Opus takes the lead at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when a teammate hits a blocker
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Teammates talk. Opus reviews.

the shared task list keeps the whole thing moving: independent tasks run in parallel, blocked tasks wait for their dependencies, and teammates message each other directly when the pieces need to line up

the full tree
> Opus 5.5 runs the main session, coordinates the work and reviews the synthesized diff before sign-off
> frontend builds the screens on Sonnet 5.5 in its own context
> backend builds the API and storage on Sonnet 5.5 in its own context
> integration prepares fixtures and tests the full flow on Sonnet 5.5
> shared tasks track ownership, progress and dependencies
> teammates message each other directly about contracts and blockers

items.title: Claude Code team member reflects on product evolution from manual approvals to trusted automation
facts: When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests.
Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products.

x_posts.author: @_catwu
x_posts.text:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!
